name: Turkic X-WMT Test — All Pairs
description: Multi-way parallel evaluation corpus from the Turkic Interlingua X-WMT test set (Mirzakhalov et al., 2021). 10 languages (Azerbaijani, Bashkir, English, Karakalpak, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Russian, Sakha/Yakut, Turkish, Uzbek), every ordered pair present (90 directions), each direction 300–1000 sentences (size varies by direction). Non-English source directions (Turkic-Turkic, Turkic→Russian) are the least-contaminated and most valuable for low-resource Turkic MT. Adds Bashkir, Karakalpak, and Sakha. MIT licensed.

segments.name: X-WMT Test
segments.purpose: MT evaluation — human-translated test set per Turkic direction; per-direction size is non-uniform, 300–1000 sentences (see pairGeneration.pairSizes); the 'size' here is the 300 nominal/floor.

download.instructions: Download test.zip (pinned to an immutable git commit). Members test/{s}-{t}/{s}-{t}.{s}.txt and .{t}.txt are one sentence per line, line-aligned. All 90 ordered pairs among the 10 languages are present.

source.citation: Mirzakhalov et al. (2021). A Large-Scale Study of Machine Translation in the Turkic Languages. EMNLP 2021.

usageRestrictions.communityNotes: Reserved as an evaluation benchmark within Champollion. doNotTrain protects benchmark integrity.

contamination.reasoning: Publicly available on GitHub since 2021. English-involving directions are more exposed; Turkic-Turkic and Turkic→Russian directions (non-English source) are substantially less likely to appear in MT/LLM training data, which is why they are prioritized.

_provenance.populatedFrom: til-mt xwmt/test.zip (pinned commit 6ac1793). Pair set (all 90) verified by direct extraction; per-direction sizes (300–1000 sentences, non-uniform) read from the sha-pinned archive and recorded in pairGeneration.pairSizes; archive sha pinned. 2026-06-23: corrected the earlier uniform-300 size pin (56 of 90 directions are larger than 300).

aze.basis: TIL X-WMT Azerbaijani is the Latin-script national standard — North Azerbaijani (azj); the only other member, South Azerbaijani (azb), is written in Arabic script.

uzb.basis: TIL X-WMT Uzbek is the Latin/Cyrillic national standard — Northern Uzbek (uzn); the only other member, Southern Uzbek (uzs), is written in Arabic script.
